stemMd: Mina: A translation should preserve the ambiguity of the original even when readers find it frustrating. Oren: When ambiguity results only from an outdated idiom, a translation should make the intended meaning explicit. They disagree most clearly about whether

options.label: A
options.textMd: translators should know the original language.

options.label: B
options.textMd: translations can preserve every sound of an original.

options.label: C
options.textMd: all translations should be easy to read.

options.label: D
options.textMd: some ambiguity in an original should be removed in translation.

options.label: E
options.textMd: outdated idioms ever occur in original texts.

explanationMd: Mina's general rule preserves original ambiguity. Oren endorses removing at least one class of ambiguity. That supplies opposite commitments on whether some original ambiguity should be removed.

distractorRationale.e: Mina has expressed no denial of this.
distractorRationale.a: Both may accept this without disagreement.
